content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal year annual data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally each June after fiscal-year data is available.", "rationale": "Firms building inventory faster than sales are overproducing relative to demand, signaling future markdowns, margin pressure, and negative earnings surprises.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growth well below sales growth)"}, {"name": "Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Quality", "construction": "Compute total accruals as (change in current assets minus change in cash) minus (change in current liabilities minus change in short-term debt minus change in taxes payable) minus depreciation (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, TXP, DP), scaled by average total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "High accruals reflect earnings driven by non-cash estimates that tend to reverse, so investors overvalue firms with low earnings persistence.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low accruals relative to cash earnings)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock", "construction": "Compute current-year capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) divided by average of the prior three years' capital expenditures, minus 1. Rank cross-sectionally each June using fiscal-year data.", "rationale": "Sharp increases in investment often reflect managerial overextrapolation of demand and empire-building, leading to poor subsequent returns as projects disappoint.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (firms cutting or holding capex flat)"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Trend", "construction": "Compute gross margin as (SALE minus COGS)/SALE for the current fiscal year and the change in this ratio versus the prior fiscal year. Rank cross-sectionally each June on the change in gross margin.", "rationale": "Improving gross margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power that the market underweights in valuations.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving gross margins)"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Momentum", "construction": "Using CRSP dividend distribution codes, flag firms that paid a cash dividend in the most recent quarter but paid none in the same quarter one year prior (dividend initiation or resumption). Form a long portfolio of these firms held for 12 months.", "rationale": "Dividend initiations credibly signal management confidence in sustainable cash flows and reduce free-cash-flow agency costs, information the market absorbs slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "firms that recently initiated or resumed dividends"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Volatility Decline", "construction": "Estimate idiosyncratic volatility as the standard deviation of residuals from a market-model regression of daily excess returns on the CRSP value-weighted index over the trailing 60 trading days. Compute the change versus the prior 60-day window. Rank cross-sectionally monthly.", "rationale": "Falling idiosyncratic volatility signals resolving uncertainty and improving information environment, which precedes positive re-rating.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (largest declines in idiosyncratic volatility)"}, {"name": "Sales-to-Price Yield", "construction": "Compute annual sales (Compustat SALE) divided by market capitalization (CRSP price times shares outstanding) measured at fiscal year end. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Sales are less subject to accounting manipulation than earnings, so high sales-per-dollar-of-price identifies cheap firms whose top-line generating capacity is underpriced.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high sales-to-price)"}, {"name": "Debt Reduction Signal", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year change in total debt (Compustat DLTT plus DLC) scaled by lagged total assets (AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Active deleveraging signals disciplined management and lowers financial distress risk and interest burden, improving future equity returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (largest debt reductions)"}, {"name": "Turnover-Adjusted Momentum", "construction": "Rank stocks on trailing 6-month return (skipping the most recent month) within terciles of average monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the same period. Favor high past-return, low-turnover stocks.", "rationale": "Low-turnover winners reflect underreaction to information among less-scrutinized stocks, producing stronger continuation than high-turnover, overly attended winners.", "higher_returns_for": "high past return combined with low share turnover"}, {"name": "Asset Growth Restraint", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year percentage change in total assets (Compustat AT). Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Rapidly expanding firms tend to overinvest and issue overpriced securities, while conservative asset growers subsequently outperform as expansion-driven mispricing corrects.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (slow or negative asset growth)"}]}
